# Embedded Tor

The iPhone app embeds C Tor 0.4.9.17 from the iCepa Tor.framework 409.17.1 release. The upstream build pins OpenSSL 3.6.5 and libevent 2.1.13. This project uses the archive built without liblzma. The library's source and license notices are available alongside this file and in the [upstream build script](https://github.com/iCepa/Tor.framework/blob/9c5df82840cd83a62b592293c2e53249ffa1e083/build-xcframework.sh).

Run `Scripts/prepare-tor.sh` on a Mac with Xcode to obtain the arm64 iPhone and Simulator libraries. The script verifies archive SHA-256 `39579058d205389ce6aaeda6b152b730bed18032ec987487218f9466e9cd6c49`, compares Tor's public embedding header with the checked-in copy, rebuilds two patched Tor objects against the release headers for each platform, and packages the two arm64 slices. For offline setup, point `TOR_RELEASE_ARCHIVE` at an existing copy. [Pinned release](https://github.com/iCepa/Tor.framework/releases/tag/409.17.1)

For an independent source build, clone Tor.framework at commit `9c5df82840cd83a62b592293c2e53249ffa1e083`, install the upstream toolchain prerequisites and run `./build-xcframework.sh -c` from that checkout. Compare the arm64 archive members in the resulting no-lzma XCFramework with the release before app linkage. Verification here covers the pinned binary archive and its iOS operation. A source-to-binary comparison is outstanding. [Upstream build instructions](https://github.com/iCepa/Tor.framework/blob/9c5df82840cd83a62b592293c2e53249ffa1e083/README.md)

Two clean runs of the preparer with Xcode 27.1 (27A9275) produced identical static archives. Their SHA-256 digests were `92d8c32bfe8e1494bbda50fd7a1c3774c8ac808671852bccadf76a4ede94524e` for arm64 iOS and `716f9678285867033e2d2cafaa7ab33a6220c8a1a908eff5689615fca9936be1` for the arm64 simulator. A different Apple compiler can change the two rebuilt objects.

## Source changes for in-process restarts

The iOS app can run Tor many times in a single process as users lock and unlock their wallets. The release's worker pool keeps its thread count and shutdown owner in process-wide static variables. The checked-in patch uses counters owned by each pool and waits for every successfully launched worker to finish before freeing its state. The second patch releases four process-wide name maps after Tor exits. A fresh Tor instance can then initialize its keyed hash tables with its own hash key. The original source files, their SHA-256 checks, and the unified diffs are in `Scripts/Tor` and `Scripts/prepare-tor.sh`. Only these two archive members are replaced. [Tor worker pool](https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/blob/a00b3e0bd288e9ae8eada8af2258a3002dfab6ff/src/lib/evloop/workqueue.c) · [Tor dispatcher name maps](https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/blob/a00b3e0bd288e9ae8eada8af2258a3002dfab6ff/src/lib/dispatch/dispatch_naming.c)

The app starts Tor with networking disabled, authenticates its private owning socket, then enables networking. A progress reading of 100 and an established circuit are required before the client releases the random loopback SOCKS endpoint. The listener accepts onion destinations only. Tor reaches entry guards and directory infrastructure while building circuits. Wallet connections send their onion destination to the local SOCKS client. The Tor state directory holds guard state for reuse and is excluded from device backups. Locking closes the owning socket. A restart or full erasure waits for the previous worker to exit. The embedded Tor thread leaves process signal handlers to the host app.

## Running the checks

The default test authenticates six network-disabled Tor instances in succession and waits for each to exit. Set `XMR_TOR_STRESS=1` in the Xcode scheme's Test environment for 100 cycles. The optional test `testLiveMainnetNodeThroughEmbeddedTor` creates an empty wallet, reaches a public Monero onion node, checks the daemon height, edits a subaddress while scanning, and verifies its label after encrypted reopen. Set `XMR_LIVE_TOR=1` in the Test environment to run this test. A network that permits Tor and a reachable Monero onion service are required.
